Md. Azizur Rahman ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Most. Hasina Jamil ----- Opposite parties
full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff petitioner filed a title suit in the Court of Assistant Judge, Damurhuda Chuadanga for declaration of title and also for declaration that the suit property is not an abandoned property. Plaintiff became the owner by purchase and has been in possession in the suit property but the property was wrongly recorded in the name of opposite party No. 1 in S.A. Khatian and the same was also wrongly enlisted as an abandoned property which creates cloud over the right, title and interest of the plaintiff Hence the plaintiff filed a suit for declaration of title and also for a declaration that the property is not an abandoned properly. 

 6. The defendant Nos. 2 and 3 namely the Government filed written statement and contended that the S.A. Khatian was rightly prepared in the name of defendant No. 1. Defendant No. 1 a non-Bengali and after her departure the property was enlisted as an abandoned property. The learned Additional District Judge, observed that though the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 claimed that the property was enlisted as an abandoned property as the defendant No. 1 left the country but the Government could not show any paper regarding that title of the defendant No. 1. Although the S.A. Khatian stood in the name of Hasina Jamil but the S.A. Khatian cannot confer any title in respect of any landed property to anybody. The learned Judge found that the suit property as per schedule of the plaint is 1.29 acres of land which appertains to plot No. 38 of C.S. Khatian No. 179 but unfortunately, the said property was not found in C.S. Khatian No. 179. The learned Judge also found from Ext. 1 the sale deed normally registered on 30.3.39 and he purchased the property of C.S. plot No. 28 and not C.S. plot No. 38 of S.A. Khatian No. 179. Accordingly the learned Judge dismissed the suit and. affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court, upon a reading of C.S. Khatian Ext. 3 (a) not Ext. 3 as the learned Judge referred the C.S. Khatian No. 179 and the hal khatian No. 422, dag as stated as 38 but quantity of land measured 1.29 acres of land was sold. The learned Judge termed the discrepancy as simple anomally. The judgment of the trial court shows that the learned Judge found that the plaintiff failed to prove his title and possession in the suit land and that the property is an abandoned property. Court of appeal below has found that the property is not an abandoned property. Government failed to prove that the property is an abandoned property. Mere recording in the S.A. Khatian could not confer any title and as such the learned Additional District Judge found that the property is not an abandoned property. Furthermore the said defendant No. 1 Hasina Jamil has not appeared and contest at the suit and did not file any written statement or adduced any evidence and as such her title could not be proved. The record of S.A. Khatian cannot also stand. Since the property is not recorded in the S.A. Khatian and the Government could not also prove the suit property as an abandoned property. The only issue that remains whether the plaintiff has been able to prove his title in the suit land. It is stated that Fakir Chand Zoarder, Tustu Zoarder and Hazu Bewa were the C.S. recorded tenants of the suit property and Ship Kumari Debi was their land lady. The said Fakir Chand Zoarder sold his share of 1.30 acres of land to Karam Ali Biswas by a registered kabala dated 30.3.39. Karam Ali Biswas died leaving behind a son Abu Hannan and 2 daughters namely Nurjahan and Forjan. Nurjahan sold .97 acres of land to the plaintiff petitioner by a registered kabala dated 12.8.68. Subsequently Forjan sold .33 acres of land to defendant No. 2 by a registered kabala dated 8.01.76. This kabala was exhibited and the plaintiff also deposed that the defendant vendors in this way transferred their shares to the plaintiffs and they are in possession of the suit property by the aforesaid purchase. P.W. 2 also stated that the plaintiff purchased the suit property and since then they are in possession by cultivating the land. P.W.3 also corroborated the evidence of P.W.1 and 2 about title and possession of the plaintiff. D.W.1 has also deposed in his cross -examination that the C.S. record was not submitted showing the name of Hasina Jamil and he has never seen Hasina Jamil. The suit property was not declared as abandoned property and he has not associated with their act declaring the property as abandoned property. The .appellate court observed that the property is not an abandoned property. Since the plaintiffs have been able to prove their title by purchase and also have been able to prove their possession, the court illegally dismissed the suit. The learned Additional District Judge misread the C.S. khatian No. 179 and found that there is no such C.S. plot No. 38 in the said C.S. Khatian. The judgment and decree passed by the courts below are not sustainable in law. 

 7. In the result, the rule is made absolute and the judgment and decree passed by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Chuadanga in Title Appeal No. 126 of 1989 and the judgment and decree dated 19.4.1989 and 24.4.1989 respectively passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Damurhuda, Chuadanga in Title Suit No. 60 of 1984 are hereby set aside. The suit is decreed and the title of the plaintiff in the suit land is declared. The S.A. Khatian in which the name of Hasina Jamil was recorded is wrong. The property is not an abandoned property.
